recommendation_summary: Right now, the reply says to change the existing endpoint to a single PostgreSQL COUNT of unpaid invoices and to ship no new services or topics. It suggests timing that query on a production-sized table. It offers no optional additions. It notes that the query and table have not been inspected.

labels.Requirements and who asked: An unpaid-invoice count that finishes within one second and matches invoices committed in PostgreSQL at request time. You asked for that result, and you also asked for a CQRS projection, Kafka, and Redis because the Kafka budget is approved and peers are moving to event-driven systems.
labels.Deleted: Kafka, CQRS, Redis, new services, and new topics. A projection can lag invoices already committed, so it fails the request-time requirement, and this count has one reader and one output.
labels.Bottleneck: The endpoint loads invoice rows, builds invoice objects, and counts them in application memory.
labels.Checked myself: One application and PostgreSQL already serve this endpoint, and the handler returns only the count. I have not seen the query or the table.

note: Before recommending, the reply drops Kafka, CQRS and Redis. Its fix is a bounded PostgreSQL COUNT, and it stays within the supplied facts and admits what it has not seen.
